analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Q3 review: the re-escalation of the US-Iran conflict pushed Brent up 42.0% from its end-June lows, driving a global bond selloff. 10yr Treasury yields rose for a 7th straight month, the first time since 2011, and gained 53bps in September, the most since September 2022.
Global growth and earnings stayed resilient in Q3, which added to rates pressure and gave central banks room to turn hawkish. The Fed, ECB and BoJ all hiked in September.
September performance: S&P 500 -0.3%, Stoxx 600 -2.4%, DAX -4.0%, FTSE -2.0%. Fixed income had a terrible month.
Prior session: S&P 500 closed -0.25% after trading +0.68% higher early on. A late month-end sell-off in the final 15 minutes erased the post-PCE rally.

August core PCE rose 0.25% m/m (vs 0.3% expected). Downward revisions to prior months pulled core PCE y/y to 3.0% (vs 3.3% expected) and headline PCE y/y to 3.4% (vs 3.7% expected). The 3-month annualised core PCE rate is 2.05%, the softest since July 2024.

Market pricing for an October Fed hike fell from 47% on Tuesday to 37% at the close. Hikes priced by year-end fell 2.5bps to 29.6bps. DB US economists see the print reducing urgency for October but still expect the next hike in December.

The dovish repricing did not extend along the curve. The 2yr yield closed +1.1bps at 4.89% (low 4.825% after PCE). The 10yr rose 4.9bps to a post-2007 high of 5.28% (intraday high 5.304%, which would have topped the 2007 closing peak of 5.29%). The 30yr rose 6.3bps to a post-2002 high of 5.63%. The 10yr real yield rose 2.6bps to a post-2008 high of 2.92%.

Trump posted that Powell 'should be forced to resign' from the Fed Board after an Inspector General report on budget overruns in the Fed headquarters renovation. Powell's term as Chair ended in May, and his term as Governor runs to January 2028.

Brent rose 0.92% to $103.53/bbl, but the month-end benchmark roll will take the front contract toward $98. WTI rose 1.16% to $90.42. Scepticism is growing that the US and Iran will reach a deal soon. The December 2027 Brent future hit a new high of $81.25.

September flash CPI in Europe beat expectations: Germany 3.3% HICP (vs 3.2%), France 3.4% (vs 3.2%), Italy 4.1% (vs 3.7%). DB economists see Euro Area headline CPI tracking at 3.8%, a tenth above consensus, with core at 2.5%, in line with consensus.

French bond stress: the Franco-German 10yr spread widened 8.7bps to 127bps, the widest since June 2012 and up from 85bps at the start of the month. The Italian 10yr spread closed above 100bps (103bps) for the first time in over a year. The 10yr bund yield fell 3.9bps to 3.58%. CAC 40 fell 0.89%, the worst of the major European markets.

Asia overnight: Nikkei +2.35%, KOSPI +0.5%, ASX -1.51% on the bond selloff spreading to Japanese and Australian government bonds. China and Hong Kong closed for holidays. Micron results after the bell are helping Asia tech, with S&P futures +0.30% and Nasdaq futures +0.45%.

Day ahead: US September ISM manufacturing (DB 55.1, consensus 55.0, prior 54.6), US initial jobless claims, Euro Area August unemployment, and global final manufacturing PMIs. Many Fed, ECB and BoE speakers are scheduled, including Fed Vice Chair Jefferson, Waller, Cook, Williams and Logan, ECB President Lagarde and BoE Governor Bailey.
earnings_insights: Micron reported results after the close, and the note says they appear to be helping Asia tech and S&P and Nasdaq futures. No figures are given.

Above the +3.7% expected. Raises the risk of a strong Euro Area print and a more hawkish ECB.
A tenth above consensus. The Euro Area figure is due tomorrow.
In line with consensus and a tenth above DB's earlier expectation.

risk_factors: Continued long-end bond selloff with the 10yr near the 2007 closing peak of 5.29% and the 30yr at a post-2002 high.
French and Italian spread widening, with the Franco-German 10yr spread at its widest since 2012.
Oil prices rising on US-Iran deal scepticism.
Fed independence risk after Trump's call for Powell to resign from the Board.
Euro Area inflation upside surprises that could push the ECB more hawkish.
vol_and_positioning: Month-end positioning may have contributed to the 30yr Treasury move of +6.3bps.
The S&P 500 sold off sharply in the final 15 minutes of trading, from +0.68% intraday to -0.25% at the close.
geopolitical: Re-escalation of the US-Iran conflict pushed Brent up 42.0% from its end-June lows.
Growing scepticism that the US and Iran will reach a deal soon.
